prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Income statement · fiscal quarters (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "USD millions" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Fiscal 2024" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Full year" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "USD millions" · longest unbreakable word 94px · one-line width 409px
  col 2: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 3: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 4: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q3" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 5: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q4" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 6: header "Full year" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 61px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare fiscal 2024 income-statement measures across four quarters and the full year, in USD millions.","reading":"Readers scan each labeled row across to compare quarters and the annual total, and scan down a column to compare measures within a period. Row labels need enough space to remain recognizable as units.","groups":["Q1–Q4 are parallel periods and should have equal widths to support comparison.","The full-year column summarizes the same measures across the four quarters and needs room for its longer heading.","The first column identifies each measure and needs more width for descriptive labels."],"keep_intact":["Quarterly and full-year numeric values, including decimal points.","Quarter identifiers Q1–Q4.","Individual words in row labels where space permits."],"may_wrap":["Long row labels can wrap at word boundaries, especially the cost-of-revenue label.","The Full year heading can wrap between words.","The existing two-level header provides height for wrapped header text."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [160, 62, 62, 62, 62, 69] · table 478×312px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 106, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 1/7 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 118px
Design r2B: widths [200, 62, 62, 62, 62, 69] · table 518×288px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 83, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 1/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 158px
Design r2C: widths [110, 62, 62, 62, 62, 69] · table 428×451px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 176, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 2/7 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 68px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
